1.title: Positive vs. Negative Self-Concept
1.stem: Write 10 statements about yourself that reflect a positive self-concept, and three that reflect a negative self-concept you sometimes catch yourself thinking. In 40-60 words, reflect on which set feels more familiar in your everyday self-talk.

1.title: Self-Concept Circle
1.stem: Draw a simple circle and divide it into sections for how you see: your body, your personality, your abilities, and your role in your family. Write 2 honest sentence in each section, then note which section was hardest to write and why.

1.title: Twenty Statements Test - Who Am I?
1.stem: Complete the sentence "I am _ _ _ _ " ten times, writing whatever comes to mind honestly, one per line. Then label each statement as Physical, Social, or Psychological. In 40-60 words, reflect on which category dominated your list and what this tells you about how you currently see yourself.

1.title: The Wheel of Emotions
1.stem: Recall a moment recently when you felt a strong, "blended" emotion (e.g., nervous excitement, angry disappointment). Name the 5 core emotions mixed together, and describe what triggered this combination.

1.title: The Feeling Wheel - Naming My Emotions
1.stem: Think of a recent moment - in class, with a friend, or during a task - when you felt something strongly. Name the specific emotion you felt (go beyond "fine," "okay," or "stressed" - be precise, e.g., "disappointed," "relieved," "embarrassed"). What triggered this emotion, and how did you respond to it?

1.title: Reframing a Challenge Optimistically
1.stem: Recall a recent personal or academic challenge. First, write how you initially felt and what you thought about yourself or the situation. Then, rewrite the same experience using a more optimistic explanatory style. What changed between the two versions?

1.title: My Optimism Test Result
1.stem: Take the free Optimism Test at psychologytoday.com/us/tests/personality/optimism-test. Note your result and reflect in 40-60 words: does it match how you see yourself, and how might your level of optimism affect the way you handle setbacks?

1.title: Why Self-Awareness Matters to Me
1.stem: In your own words, explain why self-awareness is important for you personally. Give one real example of a time being more self-aware (or not being self-aware) changed an outcome for you.

1.title: My Johari Window
1.stem: Write one thing about yourself that fits each quadrant of the Johari Window: something others and you both know about you (Open), something you keep hidden from others (Hidden), and something others may have noticed about you that you haven't fully realised yourself (Blind Spot).

1.title: My Self-Esteem Tree
1.stem: Describe your own "self-esteem tree": Roots - what gives you strength (values, family, beliefs) Trunk - your core strengths Branches - the roles you hold (student, friend, sibling, etc.) Leaves - your achievements so far Fruits - your future goals Write a short reflection (40-60 words) on which part of your tree you're proudest of.

2.title: Opening My Mind
2.stem: Imagine humans could only communicate through images instead of words. In 40-60 words, describe how your daily life - classes, friendships, family would change, and what this exercise showed you about how you normally think.

2.title: Thinking About My Thinking
2.stem: Pause right now and write down the last five things you thought about today no filtering, just be honest. For each one, note whether it was about the past, the future, yourself, or someone else, and reflect briefly on the pattern you notice.

2.title: Fast vs. Slow Thinking in My Life
2.stem: Describe 3 recent decision you made instantly, without much thought (fast thinking), and 3 you had to sit down and reason through carefully (slow thinking). Which one led to a better outcome, and why?

2.title: Reverse Thinking - Flip It Around
2.stem: If you genuinely wanted to ruin your own time management or become the worst listener in class, list at least 6 things you would do. Now flip each one into its opposite - a positive habit you will actually try to practise this month.

2.title: My Personal SWOT
2.stem: Choose one area of your own life - time management, health & wellbeing, communication skills, or your social relationships - and write an honest SWOT analysis of yourself in that area (at least 3 points under each of Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats).

2.title: Active Listening in Practice
2.stem: Ask someone (a friend or family member) to speak to you for two minutes about their day, without interrupting them. Summarise what they said in 3-4 sentences, then reflect: what was hard about listening without reacting or interrupting?

2.title: The Floor Is Yours
2.stem: Pick one of these prompts and write out what you would actually say for two minutes: (a) a motivating speech to a friend who just failed an exam, or (b) your own life goal, explained to someone who has never met you.

2.title: Stepping Into Empathy
2.stem: Describe a real moment when you understood or felt someone else's pain, struggle, or joy as if it were your own - a friend, family member, stranger, or even an animal. What did you notice, how did it make you feel, and did it change how you acted?

2.title: Treating Others Respectfully
2.stem: Name three people you genuinely respect, and for each, write one specific way you show them that respect. Then evaluate yourself honestly: are you already doing this consistently, or is there someone you plan to show more respect to going forward?

2.title: Building It Back Up - Resilience
2.stem: Describe a time something you worked hard on (a plan, project, relationship, or goal) fell apart or failed - like a card structure collapsing. How did you respond afterward, and what helped you find the energy to rebuild or start again?

3.title: Sorting My Stress
3.stem: List at least six things currently causing you stress, personally or at college. Sort them into two columns: Controllable (things you can act on through your own choices) and Uncontrollable (caused by something or someone outside your control).

3.title: Recognising My Own Stress Symptoms
3.stem: Of the four symptom categories in the book - Physical, Emotional, Cognitive, and Behavioural - identify one real symptom you personally experience under stress in each category, using your own recent experience.

3.title: The 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding Exercise
3.stem: Actually try the exercise: notice and write down 5 things you can see, 4 things you can touch, 3 things you can hear, 2 things you can smell, and 1 thing you can taste, right now. Did this shift how calm or present you felt?

3.title: Nature Journaling
3.stem: Spend 10 minutes outdoors observing nature - a tree, the sky, birds, or a garden. Write down what you noticed with your senses, and reflect: did this time in nature change your mood or stress level, even slightly?

3.title: My Go-To Coping Strategy
3.stem: From the strategies discussed in class (relaxation, exercise, sleep, social support, digital detox, etc.), describe the one you personally rely on most when stressed. Is it actually working for you, or is it more of a temporary escape? Be honest.

3.title: My Big Five Personality Profile
3.stem: Take the free Big Five personality test at bigfive-test.com and note your scores on the five traits. Do the results match how you would describe yourself?

3.title: My Personality Type in Action
3.stem: Pick one personality trait/type discussed in class (e.g., introvert/extrovert, Type A/B, or one Big Five trait) that you feel best describes you. Give a specific real- life example of this trait showing up in your behaviour.

3.title: Learning the Unwritten Rules
3.stem: Think of a real time you entered a new social setting (your first day of college, an internship, a new club, a new city). What unwritten "rules" of that group did you have to figure out, and how did you adapt while staying true to yourself?

3.title: A Different Perspective
3.stem: Describe a real conversation or friendship you've had with someone from a different cultural, linguistic, religious, or regional background than your own. What did you learn from them that you hadn't known before?

3.title: My Code of Ethics
3.stem: Describe a real situation where you had to choose between doing what was easy and doing what you believed was right. What did you decide, what value guided that decision, and would you choose the same way again?
